name: Aubrieta
grown_as: Garden aubrieta from the seed mix 'Cascade Mix' for the rockery: evergreen, low and trailing, in mixed purple, blue and red. Drawn in the typical purple. ⚠️ CHECK the colour William wants drawn.
habit: A low, dense, evergreen mat or cushion 5 to 10 cm tall and 30 to 60 cm across, spilling over stones and walls, covered in flowers in spring.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, crowded into small rosettes at the ends of short trailing stems
leaf.outline: Spoon-shaped to narrowly oval, 1 to 2.5 cm long
leaf.margin: One to three coarse teeth on each side near the tip, smooth lower down; some leaves untoothed
leaf.surface: Soft, covered in tiny star-shaped hairs, slightly felty
leaf.stalk: Very short, merging with the tapering base

flower.petals: Four, free, rounded blades on long claws hidden in the sepals
flower.colour: Purple to violet (mix: also blue, red-purple and pink)
flower.centre: A small pale yellow-green centre with stamen tips
flower.behind: Four narrow upright sepals pressed together into a tube
flower.carried: In short, loose clusters of a few flowers on short stalks, so thick they hide the mat

fruit: Small, oval to oblong, hairy pods 1 to 2 cm, held upright, with a beak left by the style; green ripening pale brown. Seeds small, oval, light brown.
seedling: Not drawn: two small round seed leaves, then tiny grey-green spoon-shaped leaves
winter: An evergreen grey-green mat of small leaves, looser after cutting back.

leaf: small spoon-shaped leaf with a few teeth near the tip only
bloom: four rounded petals in a flat cross
narrow sepals in a tube behind
young: a low spreading mat of small grey-green leaves in rosettes
flower: a low mat smothered in purple four-petalled flowers
spilling over a stone or edge
seedhead: small upright hairy pods with a beak above the mat
dormant: a low evergreen grey-green mat of small leaves

look_alikes: Arabis (rock cress) is white-flowered with greyer leaves. Phlox subulata has needle-like leaves and five-petalled flowers. Aurinia (gold dust) is yellow. Purple rock cress is another name for aubrieta.
